summary: order-service quote timeouts are downstream of a pricing-engine CPU saturation caused by a config/feature-flag change, not the market-data-service deploy. At 12:04:00, config change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100% ('Ramp Greeks v2 experiment to all traffic'). Within ~1 minute pricing-engine CPU rose from ~40% to ~99%, p99 latency from ~60ms to ~2600ms, and error_rate from ~0.2% to ~12%, with 276 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' errors and GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo warnings of 3-9s per call. The 5%->100% ramp exposed an expensive Monte-Carlo calculator (20k paths) to all quote traffic, pushing per-request compute past deadlines and beyond order-service's 2500ms client timeout (order errors begin 12:06:10). market-data-service (deployed 11:56, v5.2.0 protobuf) is healthy — flat ~40ms latency and ~45% CPU — and request_rate is flat ~645 req/s, ruling out the deploy and load growth. Restarts=0, memory flat, redis flat. Recommended: revert cfg-3120 to 5% or 0% to restore service immediately.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Greeks v2 feature-flag ramp saturated pricing-engine CPU
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100% at 12:04, exposing the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20k paths, ~3-9s per call) to all quote traffic. The added CPU work drove pricing-engine to ~99% CPU, inflating quote latency to ~2.6s past the 2000ms budget and beyond order-service's 2500ms client timeout, causing order quote timeouts.

assumptions: The GreeksV2 calculator is markedly more CPU-intensive than the default Greeks path (inferred from 3-9s compute times and the CPU jump coinciding with the ramp).

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf deploy broke quote serialization
ranked_hypotheses.statement: market-data-service v5.2.0 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' at 11:56 introduced a serialization fault that slowed decoding on pricing-engine, causing quote timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The deploy preceded the fault by ~10 minutes while CPU/latency/errors stayed normal until 12:04-12:05; market-data-service latency and CPU are completely flat (F8,F9); and the fault onsets exactly with the cfg-3120 ramp (F4,F5). Serialization on market-data would also not inflate pricing-engine CPU to 99%.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load-driven capacity saturation of pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge in quote request volume exceeded provisioned pricing-engine capacity, saturating CPU and causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat ~645 req/s with no surge (F10); the CPU jump is coincident with the feature-flag ramp, not a volume change.

facts.statement: pricing-engine CPU jumped from ~40% to ~99% at the 12:05 bucket and stayed there.
pricing-engine p99 latency jumped from ~60ms to ~2600ms at the 12:05 bucket.
pricing-engine error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~12% at the 12:05 bucket.
Config change cfg-3120 set greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04:00.
The config was applied at 12:04:16 and GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo warnings began at 12:05:21.
market-data-service latency and CPU are flat across the window despite its 11:56 deploy.
pricing-engine request_rate is flat ~645 req/s with no surge.
pricing-engine had 0 restarts and flat memory; redis-cache CPU flat.
The only deployment in the window was market-data-service v5.2.0 at 11:56 (not rolled back); pricing-engine had no deployments.

assumptions: The GreeksV2 calculator is substantially more CPU-intensive than the previously-dominant (v1/default) path; inferred from its 3-9s per-call times and the CPU jump coinciding with the flag ramp.
The config-audit gap (shard 2/3) did not hide another relevant change; pricing-engine-specific config query returned only cfg-3120.
order-service timeouts are entirely attributable to pricing-engine latency exceeding the 2500ms client timeout.

timeline.event: market-data-service v5.2.0 (protobuf quote serialization) deployed; no degradation follows.
pricing-engine logs 'config change cfg-3120 applied: flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100'.
First order-service 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' error.
Conditions persist unchanged (CPU ~99%, p99 ~2600ms); no recovery observed.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0) immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: The ramp is the trigger; reverting removes the CPU-heavy Monte-Carlo path from the bulk of traffic and should restore quote latency.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery by watching pricing-engine cpu_pct, latency_p99_ms and error_rate for several minutes after revert.
recommended_actions.rationale: CPU dropped instantly from ~40% to ~99% at the ramp, so it should return promptly; sustained ~99% would indicate a different cause.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back market-data-service v5.2.0 for this symptom; it is healthy.
recommended_actions.rationale: market-data latency/CPU are flat and its deploy precedes the onset by ~10 minutes.

recommended_actions.action: Gate the GreeksV2 flag behind a performance/canary review: benchmark the Monte-Carlo calculator cost and ramp gradually with CPU/latency SLOs.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 5%->100% jump exposed a path ~40x more CPU-expensive than the default; gradual ramp with SLO gates prevents recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on pricing-engine CPU saturation and quote latency SLO before feature-flag ramps.
recommended_actions.rationale: Saturation reached 99% with ~2.6s p99 before being reported.

data_gaps: The first all-service config_changes query (tc-003) was partial: config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond, so an unrelated config change elsewhere cannot be fully excluded (mitigated by the pricing-engine-scoped query returning only cfg-3120).
No direct profile breakdown proving the GreeksV2 calculator consumes the majority of pricing-engine CPU; this is inferred from timing correlation rather than a CPU-by-function metric.
